Title: Birol et al. (2002) Penicillin production in a fed-batch fermentor (extended Bajpai and Reuss model)

Abstract: Simulation software based on a detailed unstructured model for penicillin production in a fed-batch fermentor has been developed. The model extends the mechanistic model of Bajpai and Reuss by adding input variables such as pH, temperature, aeration rate, agitation power, and feed flow rate of substrate and introducing the CO₂ evolution term. The simulation package was then used for monitoring and fault diagnosis of a typical penicillin fermentation process. The simulator developed may be used for both research and educational purposes and is available at the web site: http://www.chee.iit.edu/~control/software.html.

Laws:
(1) [balance] Biomass concentration balance accounting for specific growth and dilution as culture volume changes.
(3) [constitutive] Specific growth rate combining hydrogen-ion inhibition, Contois limitation by glucose and oxygen, and temperature-dependent growth and death terms.
(9) [balance] Penicillin concentration balance accounting for non-growth-associated formation, hydrolysis, and dilution as culture volume changes.
(10) [constitutive] Specific penicillin production rate with substrate inhibition by glucose and biomass-dependent oxygen limitation.
(11) [balance] Glucose balance combining biomass and penicillin uptake, maintenance use, substrate feed, and volume-change dilution.
(12) [balance] Dissolved-oxygen balance combining cellular consumption, gas-liquid transfer, and volume-change dilution.
(13) [constitutive] Correlation for the oxygen mass-transfer coefficient as a function of oxygen flow and agitation power per culture volume.
(14) [balance] The culture-volume balance adds substrate feed and acid/base addition and subtracts evaporative loss.
(15) [constitutive] The temperature-dependent evaporative-loss rate is computed from culture volume and the medium’s freezing and boiling temperatures.
(16) [constitutive] The heat-generation rate is computed from biomass growth and a biomass-proportional maintenance contribution.
(17) [balance] The fermentor temperature balance accounts for feed-temperature effects, microbial heat generation, and cooling-coil heat removal.
(18) [constitutive] The carbon-dioxide evolution rate is represented as contributions from growth, maintenance, and penicillin biosynthesis.

answer.description: The model describes penicillin production in a fermentor, with a batch culture followed by fed-batch operation; the organism is not identified in the supplied text. It predicts biomass, penicillin, substrate, dissolved oxygen, culture volume, temperature, heat generation, and carbon dioxide using growth and production kinetics alongside oxygen-transfer, heat, and volume-change mechanisms. It extends the Bajpai–Reuss model with operating inputs including feed, pH, aeration, and agitation, and the software can test different sugar-feed strategies.
